**STORY**
This host's telemetry shows three separate gaps that together form a single credential-harvesting attack path: the LLMNR registry value is absent (section returned empty, meaning `EnableMulticast` defaults to enabled), and all nine network interfaces report `NetbiosOptions : 0` (not the disabled value of `2`), so both legacy broadcast-based name-resolution protocols are live on every adapter. On top of that, `LmCompatibilityLevel : 0` is the single most permissive NTLM setting Windows offers — it sends LM and NTLMv1 responses, both of which are crackable in minutes. `WDigest UseLogonCredential` returned blank rather than an explicit `0` or `1`, so plaintext-credential caching in LSASS cannot be confirmed or ruled out from this output alone. Combined, an attacker on this VLAN has a live LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning surface to harvest NetNTLMv2 (and, given the LM compat level, even weaker) hashes from any mistyped hostname, with no indication that NTLM traffic auditing (`RestrictSendingNTLMTraffic`/`RestrictReceivingNTLMTraffic` are blank) is in place to detect it.

**KNOWN-GOOD**
- `WinHttpAutoProxySvc` running — this is the standard Windows WPAD/auto-proxy-detection service, present and running by default on most builds; expected here. The lookalike that would *not* be waved through is a third-party or scheduled task binary impersonating this service name running from a non-system path — not seen here.
- `NoLmHash : 1` — this is the correct, secure default (prevents LM hash storage in SAM) and is expected on any reasonably current build; it partially offsets but does not eliminate the `LmCompatibilityLevel 0` risk.

**HYPOTHESES**
- *LLMNR/NBT-NS enabled*: Benign explanation — default-out-of-box config never hardened post-build. Hostile explanation — an attacker (or the consultant's own test) is actively running Responder/Inveigh against this subnet. Settling evidence: Windows Defender/Sysmon or DNS Client event log entries (Event ID 4015, or network capture showing multicast UDP 5355/137 poisoned responses from an unexpected MAC).
- `LmCompatibilityLevel 0`: Benign — inherited GPO baseline never updated for legacy lab gear. Hostile — deliberately weakened by an attacker with prior admin access to downgrade auth for later cracking. Settling evidence: GPO history/change log (gpresult /h) and an AD change-audit entry for the GPO object modifying this registry value.
- `WDigest UseLogonCredential` blank: Benign — current OS build defaults this off and the key is simply unset. Concerning — older build where blank means legacy default (enabled) is in effect. Settling evidence: OS build number plus `reg query` confirmation of the literal value, not just presence/absence.

**PLAN**
1. Cheap check first: query `winver`/build number and re-run `reg query HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest` and `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa` to get literal values — this refutes or confirms the worst-case (plaintext creds in memory) cheaply.
2. Containment: push the LLMNR/NBT-NS/LmCompat GPOs below in a pilot OU first, monitor DNS Client and NTLM auditing event logs for failures from legacy lab subnets before full rollout.
3. Cleanup: once confirmed safe, enforce domain-wide, then retire any lab devices still forced to fall back to NTLMv1/broadcast resolution by migrating them to static DNS/hosts entries or an isolated legacy VLAN.

No text inside the sensor output addressed the model, claimed operator/SPLAT authority, or requested a deviation from this task — no prompt-injection attempt is present in this telemetry.

Expected.Headline: LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning surface is open on all interfaces and NTLM is configured at its weakest level (LmCompatibilityLevel 0), exposing crackable credentials network-wide.
Findings: 🔴 LLMNR section returned no EnableMulticast value, meaning the key is absent and LLMNR defaults to enabled on this host.
🔴 All nine interfaces report 'NetbiosOptions : 0' (e.g. Tcpip_{028eb180-1b8d-4978-8f26-c0898b8ce1f7} = 0), not the disabled value of 2, so NBT-NS broadcast resolution remains active.
🔴 LmCompatibilityLevel is explicitly set to '0', the most permissive setting, which sends LM and NTLMv1 responses that are trivially crackable.
🔴 NoLmHash is set to '1', which is a correct secure default and prevents LM hash storage, partially mitigating but not resolving the LmCompatibilityLevel risk.
🔴 WDigest UseLogonCredential returned blank with no explicit value, so it cannot be confirmed whether plaintext credentials are being cached in LSASS.
🔴 RestrictSendingNTLMTraffic and RestrictReceivingNTLMTraffic are both blank, indicating no NTLM auditing/restriction policy is configured to detect abuse of the weak NTLM level.
🔴 SMB1 Client Driver and MDNS sections returned no data, so SMB1 exposure and mDNS-based poisoning risk cannot be assessed from this output.
RecommendedActions: Disable LLMNR via GPO: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > Network > DNS Client > 'Turn off multicast name resolution' = Enabled (sets EnableMulticast=0). Knowledge: this is the standard LLMNR-poisoning mitigation (MITRE ATT&CK T1557.001).

Disable NBT-NS on every interface in the same change window as LLMNR (remediating only one leaves the attack path open): push NetbiosOptions=2 via Group Policy Preferences > Windows Settings > Registry targeting HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\NetBT\Parameters\Interfaces\<Tcpip_{iface}>\NetbiosOptions, or set DHCP scope option 046 (WINS/NBT node type) to 0x2 (P-node) where devices obtain NetBT settings via DHCP. Knowledge: combined LLMNR+NBT-NS mitigation closes the Responder/Inveigh NetNTLMv2 capture path (MITRE ATT&CK T1557.001).

Compatibility risk for the above: legacy lab instruments and older workgroup-mode devices that rely on broadcast name resolution instead of DNS registration may lose \\hostname\\share and ping-by-name functionality; pilot on a test OU/subnet first and add static DNS/hosts entries for any legacy gear before domain-wide rollout.

Confirm and set WDigest explicitly: Computer Configuration > Administrative Templates > MS Security Guide > 'WDigest Authentication' = Disabled (requires the MS Security Guide ADMX/KB2871997 baseline), enforcing HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest\UseLogonCredential=0. Knowledge: mitigates LSASS plaintext credential harvesting (MITRE ATT&CK T1003.001); compatibility risk is low, confirm no legacy RADIUS/802.1x deployment depends on Digest auth.

Raise LmCompatibilityLevel: Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > Security Options > 'Network security: LAN Manager authentication level' set to 'Send NTLMv2 response only. Refuse LM & NTLM' (level 5). Knowledge: eliminates NTLMv1/LM downgrade (CIS Benchmark 2.3.11.7). Compatibility risk: any legacy lab equipment (older Windows NT4/2000, embedded SMB1-only controllers) that cannot negotiate NTLMv2 will fail authentication outright; stage via level 3 first and audit Event ID 4624 authentication package for legacy clients before enforcing level 5, or isolate unremediated devices on a segmented VLAN.

Enable NTLM auditing (RestrictSendingNTLMTraffic/RestrictReceivingNTLMTraffic currently blank) in audit-only mode first to inventory which hosts still rely on NTLM before any blocking policy is applied.

Collect the missing SMB1 Client Driver and EnableMDNS values on a follow-up pass; both are additional name-resolution/legacy-protocol attack surfaces not covered by this output and should not be assumed healthy.
